title: Bangkok food: 15 restaurants worth the trip
desc: Fifteen places to eat in Bangkok, from old-town noodle shops to Sukhumvit brunch spots, grouped by area.

items.title: Boonlert Egg Noodle
items.memo: Egg noodles with grilled pork and wontons; six Michelin stickers.

items.title: Dim Sum Zai
items.memo: Crispy shrimp rice rolls, xiao long bao and chili-oil dumplings by Sam Yot.

items.title: Sae Phun
items.memo: Prawn wontons with egg noodles in clear soup; years of Michelin stickers.

items.title: K. Panich
items.memo: Michelin-listed mango sticky rice; closed Sundays.

items.title: Lanzhou Noodles
items.memo: Hand-pulled noodles in five types; beef fried noodles or braised beef soup.

items.title: Ba Hao
items.memo: Scallion pancakes and beef dumplings; cocktails like the Drunken Mistress.

items.title: Urai Braised Goose
items.memo: Braised goose with a vinegar, ginger and garlic dip; split opening hours.

items.title: Naam 1608
items.memo: Old wooden riverside house on Song Wat; first-floor tables for sunset.

items.title: Dan Dan Noodle (Ari)
items.memo: Classic dan dan noodles for 105 THB; busy with the office lunch crowd.

items.title: O'ganic Concept ARI
items.memo: Farm-to-table using produce from its own farm; Korean chicken bibimbap.

items.title: Bartels Asok
items.memo: Sourdough brunch, grilled cheese and Cheeky Chicken; the larger branch.

items.title: Kenji's Lab
items.memo: Premium Japanese seafood, sushi, oysters and pasta; try sparkling sake.

items.title: NEUA.NEUR.BKK
items.memo: Extra-spicy khao soi and dried-beef fried rice; open kitchen.

items.title: Nuea Mek (Silom)
items.memo: Khao soi and Thai wagyu with sticky rice in a turquoise courtyard.

items.title: Coconut Lane (Bang Kachao)
items.memo: Cafe and stay with a terrace over palm trees; duck pad kra pao.
